LICENSE README.md dist package.json gosling.schema.d.ts index.d.ts index.js # time-i-gram **A grammar for interactive visualization of time-based data.** time-i-gram extends [Gosling.js](https://github.com/gosling-lang/gosling.js) with a temporal field type, time-aware data sources (`csv-time`, `json-time`), a time axis, time coordinate systems (calendar periods such as "week of the year" and offsets relative to an event), calendar units with aggregation, and time transforms. A visualization is a JSON spec; `embed` renders it, with zooming, brushing and linked views. This package is a single self-contained ES module: React, PixiJS, HiGlass and their CSS are bundled, so there is nothing else to install. The grammar, the editor with examples and the source code: https://github.com/vanessastoiber/time-i-gram ## Install From a CDN, nothing to install: ```js import { embed } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/time-i-gram@0.1.0/dist/index.js'; ``` With a bundler (Vite, esbuild, webpack, ...): ```bash npm install time-i-gram ``` ```js import { embed } from 'time-i-gram'; ``` ## Usage in a plain HTML page ```html
``` `embed(element, spec, options?)` returns a promise of the visualization's API (zoom to a range, subscribe to events, export images). ## Usage in Observable In an [Observable notebook](https://observablehq.com), `embed(spec)` returns an element that the cell displays: ```js embed = (await import('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/time-i-gram@0.1.0/dist/index.js')).embed ``` ```js embed({ /* a time-i-gram spec */ }) ``` In [Observable Framework](https://observablehq.com/framework/): ```js import { embed } from 'npm:time-i-gram@0.1.0'; display(await embed({ /* a time-i-gram spec */ })); ``` ## TypeScript The package includes types for `embed` and for specs: ```ts import { embed, type GoslingSpec } from 'time-i-gram'; ``` ## Citation If you use time-i-gram in your research, please cite: > V. I saved `/work/spec.json`. It renders without errors, but it only partly answers the task. The circular view and the full timeline are there. Season peaks are not marked, and the two views are not linked, because time-i-gram 0.1.0 can't do either in this design.

**What the figure shows:**
- **Circular view:** one coloured line per ISO year from 2012 to 2026, with ISO week 1 at 12 o'clock and weeks running clockwise. The radius is the weekly value. There is a year legend and a value axis.
- **Linear view:** the whole series on a calendar date axis, coloured by year.
- **Caption:** before 2020 the peak came in February–March (ISO weeks 5–12) every year. Since 2020 it has moved, with December peaks in 2022 and 2023. I checked the peak weeks against the data before writing this.

**Two requirements could not be met:**
- **R5 (linking):** time-i-gram only links views that use the same time coordinate system. The year ring uses one, the calendar timeline uses another, and the library's own code rejects links between them with a warning. I also tried building one ring per year on the calendar axis so a brush could link them. It did not render correctly, and I ran out of time.
- **R3 (peak markers):** there is no transform that finds the highest week per season and places it on the ring. The only per-season maximum (`argmax`) is the reference point of a relative time axis, which can't be combined with the ring's axis in one track. I left the peaks unmarked rather than mark them by hand, which the task rules forbid.

The warnings in the render log ("unknown data type", "No dataConfig children") also appear without any of my settings and do not affect the figure.
